questions.question: Why should flares be used with caution after an accident?

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares.
Other drivers may get confused about what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Flares can start a fire if there is spilled fuel on the ground nearby.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: It is okay to have a missing lug nut if four other lug nuts are present.
A cracked lock ring is safe if you drive under 55 mph.
A missing clamp is dangerous and must be fixed.
Welded repairs are safe for rear axle wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Cracked or bent lock rings are not safe. Welded wheel repairs are not safe.

questions.question: What must you provide to get a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: A list of countries you visited in the last 10 years.
Your employment history for the last five years.

questions.explanation: You must give your fingerprints and pass a TSA background check to get a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: What should you do when checking engine belts during a vehicle inspection?

options.text: Check that belts are tight with up to three inches of play.
You do not need to identify the water pump belt.
Identify which items are not driven by belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Identify which items are not driven by belts.
questions.explanation: Check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts for cracks and frays. Allow up to three-quarters of an inch of play in each belt. If any of these items are not belt-driven, you must identify them and check that they work properly and are not damaged or leaking.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW)?

options.text: The total weight of the vehicle and its cargo.
The total weight of the vehicle without cargo.
The total weight of the cargo only.
The maximum weight a vehicle is allowed to carry.

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of the vehicle and its cargo.
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight is the total weight of a vehicle plus everything loaded in it.

questions.question: How do you set the parking brake on newer vehicles?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.
Push in the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pull up on the steering column.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
questions.explanation: On newer vehicles with air brakes, pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob to set the parking brake. Push it in to release the brake.

questions.question: What should you do when entering fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.

questions.explanation: Avoid driving in fog if possible. If you must drive through fog, slow down before you reach it.

questions.question: When should you not use the parking brake?

options.text: When your vehicle is on a level surface.
When your vehicle is on a slight slope.
When your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
When your vehicle's other brakes are working well.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle's brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if the brakes are very hot from driving downhill or if they are wet in freezing weather. Hot brakes can be damaged, and wet brakes in freezing weather may ice up.

questions.question: What should you check on a cargo lift?

options.text: That the lift is loosely attached.
That the lift is not leaking.
That the lift is fully extended.
That the lift is the right color.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the lift is not leaking.
questions.explanation: Check the cargo lift for leaks, damage, and missing parts. The lift must be fully closed and locked tight.

questions.question: Why should you check tires regularly in very hot weather?

options.text: Air pressure may increase as temperature rises.
The tread wears down very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase as temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, so tire pressure can reach unsafe levels in very hot weather. If this happens, stop and let your tires cool. Do not let air out, as pressure will drop too low when the tires cool down.

questions.question: How many points are added to your driving record for speeding 11 to 14 mph over the speed limit?
questions.explanation: In West Virginia, speeding 11 to 14 mph over the posted speed limit adds three points to your driving record. If you get 12 or more points, your license will be suspended.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following except:

options.text: Complete the test without an accident.
Use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and signals, and complete the test without any accidents or violations. You cannot use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming drowsy while driving on a trip?

options.text: Get about three hours of sleep beforehand.
Plan ahead and include stopping points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan ahead and include stopping points.
questions.explanation: To avoid drowsy driving, get seven to eight hours of sleep before the trip, drive during the hours when you are normally awake, plan to take breaks, and exercise regularly.

questions.question: Bent lock rings:

options.text: Are not a concern in dry weather.

questions.explanation: Bent, cracked, or mismatched lock rings are dangerous and should not be used.

questions.question: When making tight turns or maneuvers, a driver should:

options.text: Open the door for a better look.

questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors regularly while driving. This is especially important when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located ____ a brake drum.
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels. The braking mechanisms that stop the vehicle are located inside the drum brake.

questions.question: When you push the brake pedal in a vehicle with air brakes, they work:

options.text: Only if the green lever on the control panel is pushed down.

questions.explanation: Air brakes take a half-second or more to work after you push the brake pedal. Air must travel through the lines first. This is different from hydraulic brakes in cars, which work immediately.

questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead to spot hazards early. Plan what you will do if a hazard becomes dangerous.

questions.question: During a trip, which of the following does not need to be checked regularly?
questions.explanation: During a trip, regularly check the gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights for problems. You do not need to check the seat cushion.

questions.question: When doing pre-trip inspections:

options.text: Do them the same way each time.
Check items in a different order each time.
Not every item needs to be inspected each time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do them the same way each time.
questions.explanation: Always do pre-trip inspections the same way. This helps you remember all the steps and ensures you do not skip anything important.

questions.question: If you see lights ahead while driving in fog, what should you know?

options.text: The lights are definitely on the road.
The lights may be a reflection.
The lights may be an optical illusion.
The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have driven off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have driven off the road.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not a reliable way to know where the road is. The lights may be from a vehicle that has left the road.

questions.question: Why should you not stare at one mirror for too long?

options.text: Looking at mirrors can make you sleepy.
You may drive a long distance without looking at the road.
The mirror may not show an accurate view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive a long distance without looking at the road.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors often, but quickly. Staring at one mirror too long means you are not watching the road ahead.

questions.question: If you have more than one driver's license, what happens?

options.text: You probably will not get caught.
You are not breaking any law.

questions.explanation: You cannot have more than one driver's license. Breaking this law can result in jail time and/or a fine up to $5,000.

questions.question: When spring brakes are active on an air brake vehicle, what should you never do?
questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are active. The combined force of the springs and air pressure could damage the brakes.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a sign of drowsiness?
questions.explanation: Signs of drowsiness include frequent blinking, eyes closing or losing focus, frequent yawning, and drifting between lanes. Drowsy driving is dangerous and must be avoided.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid during vehicle inspection, which is NOT required?

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Check that the fluid level is above the full mark.
Check that the fluid level is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During vehicle inspection, you must show where the dipstick is located and verify there is enough power steering fluid. The fluid level must be above the refill mark, not the full mark.

questions.question: What does the service brake system do?

options.text: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal during normal driving.
Applies and releases the parking brakes.
Applies and releases the emergency brake.
Applies and releases the axle brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal during normal driving.
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three separate systems: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system. The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when you use the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle near idle, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle as the engine nears idle, push in the clutch.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate must not exceed 3 psi in one minute. Faster leaking means something needs repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: If you drive a truck that requires a CDL, what about seat belts?

options.text: You do not need to wear one.
You only need to wear one if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You only need to wear one when driving a tank trailer.

questions.explanation: For safety, you must wear your seat belt at all times while operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: Before you start going down the hill
After you have started going down the hill
As far down the hill as possible
At the bottom of the hill

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start going down the hill
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before you start down a hill. This helps you control your speed without using your brakes too much.

questions.question: When entering a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Put the vehicle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before entering a curve. This helps you go through the turn at a safe speed.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required on an Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR)?
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include: the trip dates, where the trip started and ended, the route taken, odometer readings at the start and end, total distance traveled, distance in-jurisdiction, and the vehicle ID number. The number of stops is not required.

questions.question: When will an applicant be denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: If they are a U.S. citizen
If they are wanted for a misdemeanor
If they are wanted for certain felonies
If they already have a driver license

questions.correctAnswerText: If they are wanted for certain felonies
questions.explanation: Your hazardous materials endorsement can be denied or canceled if you are wanted for or convicted of certain felonies, do not have legal permanent status in the U.S., are judged mentally incompetent, or are deemed a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration.

questions.question: If you discover while driving that the ABS is not working, what should you do?

options.text: Use your parking brake to stop

questions.explanation: If the ABS is not working, your vehicle's basic braking system still works. Continue to drive and brake as you normally would.

questions.question: Engine belts should be:
questions.explanation: Check your engine belts to make sure they are tight and not worn out. The right amount of tightness varies by vehicle, so check your vehicle's specifications.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.explanation: For safety, most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have ABS. Other vehicles with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1998 must also have ABS.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent fatigue while driving?
questions.explanation: A hot, stuffy cab makes you sleepy. Open a window, use a vent, or turn on the air conditioning to keep the cab cool and alert.

questions.question: A tired driver may:

options.text: Use over-the-counter pills to stay awake
Be more careful than other drivers

questions.explanation: When tired, you cannot see or react to dangers as quickly. Your ability to make important decisions is impaired.

questions.question: What can happen if cargo is not secured on a flatbed trailer?

options.text: It can shift or fall off the trailer.
It can create a glare that blinds other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can shift or fall off the trailer.
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be secured to keep it from shifting or falling during transport.

questions.question: How long must carriers keep fuel records for IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns?
questions.explanation: Carriers must keep mileage and fuel records that support IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns for four years.

questions.question: How many driver licenses can a person have?

options.text: Two — one for cars and one for trucks.
One for each state where they plan to drive.
A car license from one state and a CDL from another.

questions.explanation: A person can have only one license. States share driver information in a computer database to prevent duplicate licenses.

questions.question: How long should it take for air pressure to build in a single air brake system?
questions.explanation: In a single air brake system, pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within three minutes after the engine reaches operating speed.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, slow down by releasing the accelerator and pushing in the clutch.

questions.question: When do spring brakes turn on?

options.text: When air pressure drops too low.
When you activate a dashboard control.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops too low.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes come on automatically when air pressure drops to an unsafe level. Exit the road safely as soon as you see the low pressure warning light.

questions.question: What can a modulating control valve control?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets you gradually apply spring brakes. The valve is controlled by a lever on the dashboard in equipped vehicles.

questions.question: What is a maneuver you may do during a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a foggy area?

options.text: Stop on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Slow down before entering fog. Use low beam headlights, do not pass others, and do not stop on the side of the road. If possible, avoid driving in fog.

questions.question: How should you do pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Differently each time, focusing on different items.
The same way each time to avoid forgetting something.
Have someone other than the driver do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time to avoid forgetting something.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This habit makes it less likely you will forget to check something important.
